events.title: Silk Road launches

research.summary: US prosecutors later alleged that Ross Ulbricht created Silk Road in approximately January 2011 and operated it as an anonymous online marketplace using Bitcoin.
research.significance: Silk Road became Bitcoin's first globally notorious commercial use case and permanently linked early crypto history with censorship resistance, darknet markets and law enforcement.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment

events.title: Mt. Gox becomes a dominant Bitcoin exchange

research.summary: Contemporary reporting described Mt. Gox as Bitcoin's most popular/dominant exchange during the 2011 boom.
research.significance: Mt. Gox's concentration made its failures systemically important to the young Bitcoin economy.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: First major Mt. Gox security crisis

research.summary: A compromised Mt. Gox account was used to dump bitcoin, sending the quoted exchange price from about $17 to pennies before trading was suspended and transactions rolled back.
research.significance: The flash crash was Bitcoin's first globally visible exchange-security crisis and exposed severe operational risk at centralized exchanges.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
BitMEX Research — June 2011 Bitcoin Flash Crash

events.title: WikiLeaks begins accepting Bitcoin donations

research.summary: WikiLeaks publicly announced that it was accepting anonymous Bitcoin donations after conventional payment channels had been restricted.
research.significance: The episode became one of the clearest early demonstrations of Bitcoin's censorship-resistant payment narrative.

sources.title: Forbes — WikiLeaks Asks for Anonymous Bitcoin Donations
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: Namecoin launches

research.summary: Namecoin was released on 18 April 2011 as an early Bitcoin-derived blockchain focused on decentralized naming.
research.significance: It was one of the first important altcoins and an early demonstration that blockchain could secure more than monetary balances.

sources.title: Namecoin — 10th anniversary of release

events.title: Casascius physical bitcoins appear

research.summary: Mike Caldwell began producing Casascius physical bitcoins: funded Bitcoin private keys embedded beneath tamper-evident holograms on physical coins.
research.significance: Casascius turned an intangible digital asset into a physical bearer collectible and became an icon of early Bitcoin culture.

sources.title: Bitcoin Annotated — Casascius Coins

events.title: Hal Finney discusses his early Bitcoin involvement publicly

research.summary: The best-known first-person account from Hal Finney, 'Bitcoin and Me,' was published in March 2013, not 2011.
research.significance: Do not retain this as a 2011 event without locating a distinct 2011 public statement that materially adds to the timeline.

sources.title: Hal Finney — Bitcoin and Me

research.notes: Likely date correction to 2013 or merge into Hal Finney biography context.

events.title: Satoshi says he has moved on to other things

research.summary: In his final known email to Mike Hearn, Satoshi wrote that he had 'moved on to other things' and that Bitcoin was in good hands with Gavin and everyone.
research.significance: The disappearance removed Bitcoin's creator from active stewardship and became one of the central mysteries and decentralization milestones in crypto history.

sources.title: Satoshi final email to Mike Hearn — moved on

events.title: Gavin Andresen discusses Bitcoin with the CIA

research.summary: Gavin Andresen gave a Bitcoin presentation at a CIA event; his June 20 forum post says the talk occurred the previous Tuesday.
research.significance: The episode captured early tension between Bitcoin's cypherpunk roots and growing government interest.

sources.title: Gavin Andresen — CIA talk follow-up

events.title: BTC-e launches

research.summary: US prosecutors describe BTC-e as a cryptocurrency exchange founded in 2011; it later became a major early venue and a focus of money-laundering enforcement.
research.significance: BTC-e is important to exchange, cybercrime and law-enforcement history.

sources.title: DOJ — BTC-e and Alexander Vinnik indictment

events.title: Silk Road drives one of Bitcoin's first large real-world use cases

research.summary: Silk Road's Bitcoin-only marketplace was a major early source of real-world transaction demand and media attention.
research.significance: Useful consequence/context of the Silk Road launch rather than a separate launch event.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: Bitcoin briefly trades above 30 dollars before crashing

research.summary: Bitcoin's 2011 rally reached roughly $32 before reversing sharply during the June Mt. Gox crisis.
research.significance: The move established Bitcoin's first major boom-bust cycle and introduced extreme crypto volatility to a wider audience.

sources.title: BitMEX Research — June 2011 Bitcoin Flash Crash
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: Mt. Gox compromised accounts trigger a dramatic flash crash

research.summary: This is the same Mt. Gox compromised-account flash crash as LORE-EVT-0016.
research.significance: Canonicalized to the first major Mt. Gox security-crisis event.

sources.title: WIRED — Bitcoin Prices Plummet on Hacked Exchange
BitMEX Research — June 2011 Bitcoin Flash Crash

events.title: Namecoin demonstrates blockchain-based naming

research.summary: Namecoin used a blockchain to register names such as .bit domains without a conventional central naming authority.
research.significance: This is the technological significance of the Namecoin launch rather than a separate event.

sources.title: Namecoin — 10th anniversary of release

events.title: Litecoin adopts Scrypt and faster block times

research.summary: Litecoin launched with Scrypt proof of work, roughly 2.5-minute block targets and an 84 million coin supply.
research.significance: These design choices distinguished Litecoin from Bitcoin but belong to the launch event's significance.

sources.title: Litecoin — 12th birthday history

events.title: WikiLeaks Bitcoin donation address becomes a censorship-resistance symbol

research.summary: WikiLeaks' Bitcoin donation address became a lasting symbol in debates over financial censorship and permissionless payments.
research.significance: Contextual cultural significance of the canonical WikiLeaks donation event.

sources.title: Forbes — WikiLeaks Asks for Anonymous Bitcoin Donations
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: Silk Road's marketplace economy drives Bitcoin transaction growth

research.summary: This row describes the same Silk Road growth/use-case story as LORE-EVT-0014 and LORE-EVT-0424.
research.significance: Keep only as contextual evidence if needed for a Silk Road chapter.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment
WIRED — The Rise and Fall of Bitcoin

events.title: SolidCoin and early altcoin experiments show rapid fork culture

research.summary: SolidCoin's original announcement states that the chain officially started on 20 August 2011 as an early Bitcoin-derived alternative currency.
research.significance: SolidCoin is a useful deep-cut example of the rapid fork/altcoin experimentation that began soon after Bitcoin gained traction.

sources.title: SolidCoin original announcement

events.title: Bitcoin mining shifts decisively from CPUs toward GPUs

research.summary: GPU software such as Laszlo Hanyecz's 2010 OpenCL miner accelerated Bitcoin's transition away from CPU-only mining; by 2011 GPU mining was widespread.
research.significance: This is an important mining-era transition, but not one unique 2011-day event.

sources.title: Laszlo GPU mining thread

events.title: Early Bitcoin pools reduce variance for individual miners

research.summary: Mining pools such as Slush Pool and DeepBit reduced payout variance by sharing block rewards among participating miners.
research.significance: Pooling changed mining from isolated lottery-like solo mining into organized industrial cooperation.

sources.title: Slush pooled mining announcement
DeepBit contemporary mining-pool discussion

events.title: Early Bitcoin whale wallets become subjects of public blockchain analysis

research.summary: Public blockchains made large address balances and old wallet movements observable, creating the enduring idea of Bitcoin 'whales.'
research.significance: This is a recurring phenomenon rather than a single 2011 event and should not be scored as-is.
research.notes: Replace with specific historically documented whale movements if a card-worthy event is needed.

events.title: Deepbit becomes one of the largest early Bitcoin mining pools

research.summary: DeepBit was one of the largest mining pools during Bitcoin's first major growth cycle.
research.significance: Useful mining-concentration context; retain unless a stronger exact milestone is identified.

sources.title: DeepBit contemporary mining-pool discussion

events.title: Bitcoin faucets and giveaways become common growth tools

research.summary: Bitcoin faucets became a common method of distributing small amounts of BTC to newcomers following Gavin Andresen's 2010 faucet.
research.significance: This trend descends from the canonical Faucet event.

sources.title: Bitcoin Faucet thread

events.title: Roger Ver becomes known as Bitcoin Jesus

research.summary: Roger Ver began acquiring and aggressively promoting Bitcoin in 2011 and later became widely known as 'Bitcoin Jesus.'
research.significance: He became one of early Bitcoin's most recognizable evangelists, though the nickname has no single verified 2011 origin date.

sources.title: DOJ — Roger Ver described as Bitcoin Jesus

research.notes: Do not state that the nickname itself was coined in 2011.

events.title: Ross Ulbricht creates Silk Road under Dread Pirate Roberts identity

research.summary: Ross Ulbricht created Silk Road and operated it under the Dread Pirate Roberts identity, according to the later federal case.
research.significance: The human/identity angle belongs within the canonical Silk Road event unless card editorial chooses a separate Ulbricht story.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment

events.title: Silk Road forum reputation system builds trust in anonymous markets

research.summary: Silk Road used marketplace reputation, escrow and pseudonymous accounts to create trust among strangers.
research.significance: Important marketplace-design context, but not a single cleanly dated milestone.

sources.title: DOJ — Ross Ulbricht / Silk Road indictment

events.title: BitInstant becomes a major early fiat on-ramp

research.summary: BitInstant was announced on 23 August 2011 as a service designed to move funds rapidly into Bitcoin exchanges.
research.significance: It became an important early fiat on-ramp and part of the first wave of Bitcoin financial infrastructure.

sources.title: Bitcoin Wiki — BitInstant history

events.title: Charlie Lee creates Litecoin while working at Google

research.summary: Charlie Lee created Litecoin while employed at Google and announced it publicly in October 2011.
research.significance: The personal-origin story is important, but it overlaps heavily with the canonical Litecoin launch.

sources.title: Litecoin — 12th birthday history

events.title: Litecoin launches

research.summary: Charlie Lee announced Litecoin on 9 October 2011; Litecoin's genesis block was mined about three days later, and the planned public launch time was 13 October.
research.significance: Litecoin became the longest-lived major early Bitcoin-derived altcoin and popularized Scrypt, faster blocks and a 'digital silver' narrative.

sources.title: Litecoin — How was Litecoin created?
Litecoin — 12th birthday history
